outcome: AI services, models and training data across the cloud estate are discovered and mapped to an owner who can confirm they belong.
overview: Teams adopt AI services faster than any governance process can follow: a model endpoint enabled for a prototype, a training job reading a production dataset, a vector store nobody classified. Prisma Cloud AI security posture discovers those assets across cloud accounts and reports what data they touch and who can reach them. The first output is an inventory, and it is usually surprising — but this is a discovery and governance control, not a model-safety control, so it shows what exists and how exposed it is rather than whether a model behaves well.

benefits.text: AI services, model endpoints and training data stores across cloud accounts are discovered and inventoried
benefits.limits: Discovery covers the managed AI services the connectors support; a self-hosted model on a virtual machine appears as a workload and not as an AI asset

benefits.text: Exposure of AI assets — public reachability, over-broad entitlements, sensitive training data — is reported
benefits.limits: Sensitivity depends on data classification; where the estate has none, the platform reports exposure without knowing what is exposed

benefits.text: AI adoption becomes a governed inventory rather than a set of individual decisions
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. The control plane is vendor-operated, so tenant region and log residency are design decisions to be made and recorded explicitly rather than properties of the product

residency: Vendor-operated control plane; asset metadata leaves the customer tenancy, and the tenant region is chosen and recorded at design

notFor.situation: An estate with no managed cloud AI services in use
notFor.why: There is nothing for the discovery connectors to find, and self-hosted models are covered as ordinary workloads

notFor.situation: An organisation looking for model behaviour or output safety controls
notFor.why: This is a posture and exposure control; it does not evaluate what a model says or does

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 4–8 weeks to an inventory with exposure findings routed to owners
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional governance review cycle with the customer’s AI owner.
1) Connect — read-only account connections across the estate in scope
2) Discover — AI asset inventory with the data each reads and the identities that reach it
3) Assess — exposure findings placed on the shared severity scale and prioritised by classification
4) Route and hand over — findings routed to owners, governance review cycle established
deliverables: Every connected account contributes to the AI asset inventory, or is listed as an explicit exclusion
Each discovered asset carries the data it reads and the identities that can reach it
The inventory distinguishes supported managed services from workloads discovery cannot classify as AI
effort: 4–8 weeks to an inventory with exposure findings routed to owners
